Random generation of paired counts

Source: R/rbicount.R
rbicount.Rd

rbicount() draws pairs of counts (y1, y2) from the generating model of the bipois and binegbin families, and returns the three latent components of each pair with the pair. The arguments are the native parameters of the families, in the order and under the names that mfd_to_dpars() returns them.

Usage

rbicount(
  n,
  mu,
  lambdaone,
  lambdatwo,
  shapes = NULL,
  shapexone = NULL,
  shapextwo = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Number of pairs to draw. If length(n) > 1, the length of n is taken to be the number required, as in stats::rnbinom().

mu

Mean of the shared component Ns.

lambdaone, lambdatwo

Means of the source-exclusive components N1 and N2.

shapes, shapexone, shapextwo

NB2 (inverse) dispersion parameters of Ns, N1, and N2. Supply all three for negative-binomial components (the binegbin family), or none for Poisson components (the bipois family).

Value

A data frame with n rows and five integer columns: y1 and y2, the two recorded counts, followed by Ns, N1, and N2, the shared component and the two exclusive components, with y1 = Ns + N1 and y2 = Ns + N2 on every row.

Details

Both families construct the pair by trivariate reduction. Three independent latent counts are drawn: the shared component Ns, recorded by both sources, with mean mu; and the source-exclusive components N1 and N2, each recorded by one source alone, with means lambdaone and lambdatwo. The recorded counts are

$$y_1 = N_s + N_1, \qquad y_2 = N_s + N_2,$$

so that \(E[y_1] = \mu + \lambda_1\), \(E[y_2] = \mu + \lambda_2\), and \(\mathrm{Cov}(y_1, y_2) = \mathrm{Var}(N_s)\).

With the three dispersions supplied, each component is negative binomial in the NB2 parameterisation, drawn by rnbinom(size = phi, mu = m). A component with mean \(m\) and dispersion \(\phi\) has variance \(m + m^2/\phi\), so a small \(\phi\) gives a heavy tail and \(\phi = \infty\) gives the Poisson limit. The dispersion of Ns is shapes, of N1 is shapexone, and of N2 is shapextwo. With all three dispersions NULL, each component is Poisson, with variance equal to its mean. Supplying some of the dispersions and not others stops with an error, because neither family has a mixture of Poisson and negative-binomial components.

Each parameter is recycled to length n, as by stats::rnbinom(), so a parameter may be a single value or a vector with one value per pair. The list returned by mfd_to_dpars() has elements named mu, lambdaone, lambdatwo, and, when overdispersions are supplied to it, shapes, shapexone, and shapextwo, so do.call(rbicount, c(list(n = n), pars)) draws pairs at the native parameters pars (see Examples). The overdispersion \(\kappa = 0\) gives shapes = Inf in mfd_to_dpars(), and rbicount() then draws a Poisson component.

The components are drawn by the code that posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() uses for each posterior draw, so a pair simulated by rbicount() and a posterior predictive draw at the same parameter values have the same distribution.

To simulate a partially paired design, draw an observation indicator, such as y1_obs <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.2), and set y1 to -1 on the rows where y1_obs is 0 before fitting with bipois_partialobs() or binegbin_partialobs(). The columns Ns and N1 keep the values from which the unrecorded y1 would have been formed.

See also

mfd_to_dpars() for the native parameters at given values of the midpoint, congruence, and source bias; posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() for draws of the pair from a fitted model.

Examples

set.seed(1)

# Poisson components, as in bipois()
rbicount(5, mu = 4, lambdaone = 1, lambdatwo = 2)
#>   y1 y2 Ns N1 N2
#> 1  5  4  3  2  1
#> 2  6  4  3  3  1
#> 3  5  7  4  1  3
#> 4  8  8  7  1  1
#> 5  2  5  2  0  3

# Negative-binomial components, as in binegbin(). The covariance of the
# two counts is Var(Ns) = 4 + 4^2/2 = 12.
d <- rbicount(
  10000,
  mu        = 4,
  lambdaone = 1,
  lambdatwo = 2,
  shapes    = 2,
  shapexone = 4,
  shapextwo = 4
)
cov(d$y1, d$y2)
#> [1] 11.58208

# Parameters from the midpoint, congruence, and source bias
pars <- mfd_to_dpars(
  M      = 5,
  f      = 0.7,
  delta  = atanh(0.3),
  kappas = 0.5,
  kappax = 0.5
)
d <- do.call(rbicount, c(list(n = 100), pars))

# A partially paired design. y2 is recorded on every unit, and y1 on about
# 20% of units.
d$y1_obs  <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, 0.2)
d$y1_true <- d$y1
d$y1[d$y1_obs == 0] <- -1L
head(d)
#>   y1 y2 Ns N1 N2 y1_obs y1_true
#> 1 -1  6  5  0  1      0       5
#> 2 -1  4  4  1  0      0       5
#> 3 -1  8  8 10  0      0      18
#> 4 -1  6  4  3  2      0       7
#> 5 -1  3  3  0  0      0       3
#> 6 -1  4  4  1  0      0       5

# Thirty units in each of three treatments that differ in congruence
if (requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  units <- data.frame(
    treatment = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 30)
  )
  units |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      f = c(a = 0.5, b = 0.7, c = 0.9)[treatment],
      as.data.frame(
        mfd_to_dpars(
          M      = 5,
          f      = f,
          delta  = 0,
          kappas = 0.5,
          kappax = 0.5
        )
      ),
      rbicount(
        dplyr::n(),
        mu,
        lambdaone,
        lambdatwo,
        shapes,
        shapexone,
        shapextwo
      )
    ) |>
    head()
}
#>   treatment   f  mu lambdaone lambdatwo shapes shapexone shapextwo y1 y2 Ns N1
#> 1         a 0.5 2.5       2.5       2.5      4         4         4  7  7  6  1
#> 2         a 0.5 2.5       2.5       2.5      4         4         4  5  7  3  2
#> 3         a 0.5 2.5       2.5       2.5      4         4         4  7  5  3  4
#> 4         a 0.5 2.5       2.5       2.5      4         4         4  7  2  1  6
#> 5         a 0.5 2.5       2.5       2.5      4         4         4  4  3  1  3
#> 6         a 0.5 2.5       2.5       2.5      4         4         4  5  4  3  2
#>   N2
#> 1  1
#> 2  4
#> 3  2
#> 4  1
#> 5  2
#> 6  1
